out_items.name: Hands clean and properly washed

violations.title: When to Wash
violations.observation: A food employee failed to wash his or her hands before engaging in food preparation, after touching bare human body parts, after coughing, sneezing, eating, after handling soiled utensils, or after engaging in any activity that could contaminate the hands.
violations.corrective_action: ALL food employees shall wash their hands OFTEN especially after handling trash, using the restroom, handling raw meats, handling soiled equipment and utensils, BEFORE putting on clean gloves, etc. Proper handwashing frequencies will aid in the reduction of foodborne illness. EHS DISCUSSED WITH PIC THAT AFTER EACH TIME AN ACTIVITY IN THE KITCHEN IS COMPLETED (PREPPING FOOD, CUTTING FOOD, HANDLING MONEY, ECT.) THE EMPLOYEE SHOULD WASH THIER HANDS. PIC HAD EMPLOYEE WASH HAND PROPERLY.

violations.title: Cleaning Procedure
violations.observation: Observed food employee wash hands without using soap and dried hands on their pants.
violations.corrective_action: Food employees shall wash their hands and exposed portions of their arms by: 1) discarding used gloves; 2) rinsing under warm running water; 3) applying soap; 4) rubbing together for at least 10-15 seconds; 5) rinsing thoroughly under warm running water; and 6) drying with paper towels or air drying device. EHS DISCUSSED WITH PIC THAT ALL EMPLOYEES SHOULD KNOW HOW TO PROPERLY WASH HANDS. EHS DISCUSSED PROPER HAND WASHING PROCEDURES WITH PIC AND HOW TO IMPLEMENT CORRECT HAND WASHING PROCEDURES AT FACILITY.

out_items.name: Food separated and protected

violations.title: Separation of Raw Animal and RTE Foods
violations.observation: Raw animal food storage, preparation, holding or display conducted in a manner that may cause cross contamination of ready-to-eat food as follows: Cooked chicken tenders were being stored directly on top of raw beef in the 2DR UPR Supera on cookline.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from cross contamination by separating raw animal foods like poultry, beef, pork, seafood, and eggs from cooked foods, ready-to- eat foods, washed produce, etc during storage, preparation, holding or display. Raw foods shall be stored on shelving units BELOW or SEPARATED from all cooked foods, commercially processed foods, washed produce, leftover foods, etc. EHS DISCUSSED WITH PIC THAT RAW FOODS SHOULD BE STORED ABOVE RAW FOODS. READY TO EAT FOODS SHOULD ALSO NEVER BE STORED DIRECTLY ON TOP OF RAW FOODS. PIC MOVED THE READY TO EAT CHICKEN TENDERS TO A DIFFERENT SHELF IN THE SUPERA COOLER.

out_items.name: Proper hot holding temperatures

violations.title: Hot Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed hot holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: French fries (120F) and fried yuca (112F) were not temping properly at 135F or above at time of inspection.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature conrol for safety food shall be held hot at a temperature of 135F or above unless the permit holder is using 'time as the public health control' as specified under 3-501.19. PIC THREW AWAY ALL HOT HOLDING FOODS NOT TEMPING PROPERLY AT TIME OF INSPECTION.

out_items.name: Proper cold holding temperatures

violations.title: Cold Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed cold holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: Sliced tomatoes (50F), cooked chicken (60F) and shredded lettuce in the 1DR prep top unit were temping above the proper 41F. Yuca was being stored at room temperature at 74F at time of inspection.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be held cold at a temperature of 41F or below unless the permit holder is using 'time as public health control as specified under section 3-501.19 to limit bacteria growth. EHS DISCUSSED WITH PIC THAT ALL COLD FOODS MUST BE KEPT AT 41F OR BELOW AT ALL TIMES TO BE SAFE TO EAT. DUE TO FOOD ONLY BEING IN THE 1DR PREP TOP UNIT FOR 3 HOURS, PIC HAD EMPLOYEE MOVE ALL FOODS NOT TEMPING PROPERLY TO A NEAR BY COOLER TO COOL DOWN ALL FOODS SO THEY CAN STILL BE USED. PIC ALSO MOVED THE YUCA INTO A NEAR BY COOLER TO COOL BACK TO 41F OR BELOW. CHICKEN PLACE, THE (Inspection Date: 08/06/2026) Page 2 of 4

out_items.name: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control

violations.title: Methods to Facilitate Proper Cooling
violations.observation: The following methods used for cooling were not adequate to facilitate proper cooling: Employee was storing the cooked chicken used for sandwiches at room temperature to cool after it hit the 135F temperature and it had begun the cooling process. The cooked chicken was temping at 88F at time of inspection, after sitting out for 3 plus hours.
violations.corrective_action: Cooling hot foods shall be accomplished as follows: 1) placing the food in shallow pans; 2) separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; 3) using rapid cooling equipment; 4) stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; 5) using containers that facilitate heat transfer; 6) adding ice as an ingredient; or other effective methods. Food containers placed in cooling and cold equipment to cool shall be: 1) arranged in the equipment to provide maximum heat transfer through the containers walls, and 2) loosely covered or uncovered as long as protected from contamination to facilitate heat transfer from the surface of the food. EHS DISCUSSED WITH PIC THE PROPER WAYS TO COOL FOOD. PIC THREW AWAY CHICKEN THAT WAS IMPROPERLY COOLING.

violations.title: Frozen food stored frozen
violations.observation: Frozen foods not maintained at proper temperature. Frozen yuca in the walk-in freezer were temping at 39F at time of inspection. Frozen frech fries in the 2DR UPR Supera cooler on cook line was temping at 39F.
violations.corrective_action: Stored frozen foods shall be maintained frozen. EHS DISCUSSED WITH PIC THAT ALL FOOD THAT NEED TO BE STORED AND KEPT FROZEN SHOULD MAINTAIN A TEMPERATURE OF 32F OR BELOW. PIC IS WORKING ON A SOLUTION TO MAKE SURE ALL FROZEN FOODS STAY FROZEN BEFORE USE. CHICKEN PLACE, THE (Inspection Date: 08/06/2026) Page 3 of 4

out_items.name: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage, and display

violations.title: Food Storage 6 inches above Floor
violations.observation: Food stored on the floor and/or food stored less than 6 inches off the floor.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from contamination by storing the food at least 6 inches off the floor on approved shelving units or dunnage racks. Milk crates, soda crates, or bread racks are not suitable for food storage. PLEASE MAKE SURE TO STORE ALL FOODS AT LEAST 6 INCHES OFF THE GROUND AT ALL TIMES. PLEASE MAKE SURE ALL FOOD IS BEING STORED OFF THE GROUND BY NEXT ROUTINE INSPECTION.

violations.title: Food Storage No Contamination
violations.observation: Food stored in a location where it is subject to splash, dust or other contamination as follows: raw produce and cilantro was being stored in an area that is subject to splashes and dust. Raw chicken getting prepped at the 3 vat sink was also subject to splashes due to employee attempting to clean a cutting board at the 3 vat sink.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from contamination by storing the food where it is not exposed to splash, dust or other contamination. PIC HAD EMPLOYEE REMOVE THE RAW PRODUCE AND CILANTRO INTO THE OUTSIDE WALK-IN COOLER AND OUT OF AREA THAT IS SUBJECT TO SPLASHES AND DIRT. PIC EXPLAINED TO EMPLOYEES THAT THEY ALSO CANNOT WASH DISHES IN THE 3 VAT SINK WHILE ACTIVELY PREPPING FOOD. EMPLOYEE IMMEDIATELY STOPPED WASHING THE CUTTING BORD UNTIL THE PREP WAS COMPLETED.

out_items.name: Wiping cloths properly used and stored

violations.title: Wiping Cloths Stored in Sanitizer Solution
violations.observation: Wet wiping cloths used for wiping counters and other equipment surfaces were observed stored on the counter.
violations.corrective_action: Wet wiping cloths are to be used for wiping counters and other equipment surfaces and are to be held in a chemical sanitizer solution at the appropriate concentration between uses. EHS DISCUSSED WITH PIC THAT ALL SANITIZER TOWELS MUST BE STORED IN THE SANITIZER SOLUTION BUCKETS IN BETWEEN USES AND CANNOT BE STORED ON PREP TABLES.

out_items.name: In-use utensils properly stored

violations.title: In-Use Utensils Proper Storage
violations.observation: Dispensing and/or in-use utensils improperly stored between use as follows: a knife was being stored between the wall and a prep table near the 3 vat sink.
violations.corrective_action: During pauses in food preparation or dispensing, food utensils shall be stored in one of the following manners: 1) in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container, 2) in food that is not time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food with their handles above the top of the food within containers or equipment that can be closed, 3) on a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized, 4) in running water of sufficient velocity to flush particulates to the drain, 5) in a clean, protected location if the utensils are used only with a food that is NOT TCS food, or 6) in a container of water if the water is maintained at a temperature of at least 135F and the container is cleaned frequently. EHS DISCUSSED WITH PIC THE PROPER WAY TO STORE IN USE UTENSILS AND EMPLOYEE MOVED KNIFE TO BE PROPERLY WASHED, RINSED AND SANITIZED BEFORE USING AGAIN.

out_items.name: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used

violations.title: Equipment, Maintain in Good Repair/Condition
violations.observation: The following refrigeration unit is not operating properly and is unable to maintain cold food at or below 41F: The 1DR prep top unit was temping at 65F at time of inspection. The walk-in freezer was temping at 60F at time of inspection. 2DR UPR Supera freezer was temping at 40F at time of inspection.
violations.corrective_action: Repair/adjust the unit so it is able to maintain foods at or below 41F. Do not use the unit to store time/temperature control for safety foods while it is not operating properly. EHS DISCUSSED WITH PIC THAT ALL REFRIGERATION UNITS SHOULD BE TEMPING AT 41F AND ALL FREEZER UNITS SHOULD BE TEMPING AT 32F OR BELOW AT ALL TIMES. PIC HAD EMPLOYEES MOVE ALL FOOD FROM THE BROKEN PREP TOP TO A NEAR BY COOLER. PIC WILL CALL TECHNICIAN TO FIX ALL 3 UNITS AND EHS WILL CONDUCT A MAKE SURE UNITS HAS BEEN FIXED.

violations.title: Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, Design/Construction
violations.observation: Milk crate(s) found used for the following purpose(s): Multiple food items in and outside of the OUTSIDE WALK-IN COOLER were being stored in milk crates.
violations.corrective_action: Milk crates, soda crates, and/or bread racks are not designed to store or elevate food, equipment, utensils, clean linens, and single-service items. Provide only ANSI-certified (such as NSF-listed) shelving units, storage units, or dunnage racks. EHS DISCUSSED WITH PIC THAT ALL FOODS SHOULD BE STORED IN NSF APPROVED CONTAINERS THAT CAN BE PROPERLY WASHED, RINSED AND SANITIZED. PLEASE REMOVE ALL MILK CRATES FROM FACILITY BY TIME OF NEXT ROUTINE INSPECTION.

out_items.name: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures and records

violations.title: TPHC, Food Marked with 4 Hour End Point
violations.observation: The following food item(s) for which time rather than temperature is used as a control is not marked or otherwise identified to indicate the time that is 4 hours past the point in time when the food is removed from temperature control: OBSERVED SALADS ON TPHC UNDER COUNTER TO BE LABELED WITH START TIME INSTEAD OF END TIME.
violations.corrective_action: If time only, rather than time in accordance with temperature control, up to a maximum of 4 hours, is used as the public health control the food shall: 1) have an initial temperature of 41F or less if removed from cold holding temperature OR 135F or above if removed from hot holding temperature control, 2) be marked or otherwise identified to indicate the time that is 4 hours past the point in time when the food is removed from temperature control, 3) be cooked and served, served if ready-to-eat, or discarded within 4 hours from the point in time when the food is removed from temperature control, and 4) be discarded if unmarked or marked to exceed a 4 hour limit. CDI: EMPLOYEES RE-EDUCATED. SALADS LABELED WITH END TIME.

PLEASE VISIT https://www.fairfaxcounty.gov/health/food/operators/consumer-advisory AND USE TO CREATE A CONSUMER ADVISORY FOR THE ABOVE ITEMS ON OR BEFORE FEBRUARY 23, 2026.. THESE FOOD ITEMS NEED TO HAVE AN ASTERISK NEXT TO THEM AND THE DISCLOSURE AND REMINDER STATEMENT ON THE TO GO MENU. CHICKEN PLACE, THE (Inspection Date: 02/13/2026) Page 2 of 4

out_items.name: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage, and display

violations.title: Miscellaneous Source Contamination
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were found subject to contamination after receipt and during storage due to the condition as described: OBSERVED DOZENS OF BOXES DELIVERED FOOD STORED IN UNSEALED MAKESHIFT BUILDING OFF THE BACK OF THE RESTAURANT. OBSERVED A WALK-IN COOLER, STAND-UP FREEZER, FOOD PREPARATION, AND DRY STORAGE SHED IN THIS AREA. STRUCTURE IS NOT WATER PROOF, IS LEAKING DUE TO SNOW MELT, THE WALLS ARE MADE OF WIRE FENCING WITH RAW WOOD, PLASTIC, AND STORE POSTERS. GAPS ARE PRESENT ALONG NEARLY EVERY SURFACE. THE INSIDE OF THE STRUCTURE CAN BE ACCESSED BY CLIMBING, AN ENTRANCE IN THE FENCE NEAR THE DUMPSTERS, AND FROM THE INSIDE OF THE BUILDING.

PLEASE SUBMIT PLANS TO FAIRFAX COUNTY HEALTH DEPARTMENT FOR AN APPROVED STRUCTURE BY MARCH 13, 2026. MOVE ALL FOOD INDOOR THE APPROVED BUILDING.
